requirements.quote:
content-length header field.  A request or response is also malformed
   if the value of a content-length header field does not equal the sum
   of the DATA frame payload lengths that form the content, unless the
   message is defined as having no content.  For example, 204 or 304
   responses contain no content, as does the response to a HEAD request.
requirements.condition: A request or response has a content-length field, includes message content, and its value differs from the sum of the payload lengths of the DATA frames forming that content.
requirements.required_behavior: Classify the request or response as malformed.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation test can compare the declared content length with the aggregate DATA payload length and observe malformed-message classification.

requirements.quote:
A response that is defined to have no content, as described in
   Section 6.4.1 of [HTTP], MAY have a non-zero content-length header
   field, even though no content is included in DATA frames.
requirements.condition: A response is defined to have no content and no content is included in DATA frames.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the response to carry a non-zero content-length field.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can send a no-content response with a non-zero content-length field and no DATA content and verify that this fact alone is accepted.

requirements.quote:
Intermediaries that process HTTP requests or responses (i.e., any
   intermediary not acting as a tunnel) MUST NOT forward a malformed
   request or response.  Malformed requests or responses that are
   detected MUST be treated as a stream error (Section 5.4.2) of type
   PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: An intermediary processes, rather than tunnels, a request or response that is malformed.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Forward the malformed request or response.
requirements.why_checkable: A forwarding test can inject a malformed message and observe whether a processing intermediary forwards it.

requirements.quote:
Intermediaries that process HTTP requests or responses (i.e., any
   intermediary not acting as a tunnel) MUST NOT forward a malformed
   request or response.  Malformed requests or responses that are
   detected MUST be treated as a stream error (Section 5.4.2) of type
   PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: A malformed request or response is detected.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the malformed message as a stream error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can submit a malformed message and verify the stream-level error type emitted by the implementation.

requirements.quote:
For malformed requests, a server MAY send an HTTP response prior to
   closing or resetting the stream.  Clients MUST NOT accept a malformed
   response.
requirements.condition: A server receives a malformed request.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the server to send an HTTP response before closing or resetting the stream.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can verify that a server is allowed to emit a response before its stream close or reset action.

requirements.quote:
For malformed requests, a server MAY send an HTTP response prior to
   closing or resetting the stream.  Clients MUST NOT accept a malformed
   response.
requirements.condition: A client receives a malformed response.
requirements.why_checkable: A client test can deliver a malformed response and observe whether it is accepted for normal processing.

requirements.quote:
before detecting errors.  A server MAY generate a final response
   before receiving an entire request when the response does not depend
   on the remainder of the request being correct.
requirements.condition: A server has not received the entire request, and its response does not depend on the remainder of the request being correct.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the server to generate a final response before the entire request is received.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can withhold the remainder of a request and determine whether the server may produce an independent final response early.

requirements.quote:
HTTP fields (Section 5 of [HTTP]) are conveyed by HTTP/2 in the
   HEADERS, CONTINUATION, and PUSH_PROMISE frames, compressed with HPACK
   [COMPRESSION].
requirements.condition: HTTP fields are conveyed in an HTTP/2 message.
requirements.required_behavior: Convey the fields in HEADERS, CONTINUATION, or PUSH_PROMISE frames using HPACK compression.
requirements.why_checkable: Frame inspection can verify the frame types and HPACK encoding used to carry HTTP fields.

requirements.quote:
Field names MUST be converted to lowercase when constructing an
   HTTP/2 message.
requirements.condition: An implementation constructs an HTTP/2 message.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Construct the message with uppercase characters in field names.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded field names in a constructed message can be inspected for uppercase characters.

requirements.quote:
implementations SHOULD validate field names and values according to
   their definitions in Sections 5.1 and 5.5 of [HTTP], respectively,
   and treat messages that contain prohibited characters as malformed
   (Section 8.1.1).
requirements.condition: An HTTP/2 implementation processes field names and values.
requirements.required_behavior: Validate field names and values according to their respective HTTP definitions and classify messages containing prohibited characters as malformed.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can supply valid and prohibited field characters and inspect validation and malformed-message classification.

requirements.quote:
*  A field name MUST NOT contain characters in the ranges 0x00-0x20,
      0x41-0x5a, or 0x7f-0xff (all ranges inclusive).  This specifically
      excludes all non-visible ASCII characters, ASCII SP (0x20), and
      uppercase characters ('A' to 'Z', ASCII 0x41 to 0x5a).
requirements.condition: An implementation validates an HTTP/2 field name.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Allow the field name to contain any character in the inclusive ranges 0x00-0x20, 0x41-0x5a, or 0x7f-0xff.
requirements.why_checkable: Boundary and representative byte values from each prohibited range can be injected into field names.

requirements.quote:
*  With the exception of pseudo-header fields (Section 8.3), which
      have a name that starts with a single colon, field names MUST NOT
      include a colon (ASCII COLON, 0x3a).
requirements.condition: A field name is not the name of a pseudo-header field that starts with a single colon.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Allow the field name to include ASCII COLON (0x3a).
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can place a colon at positions in ordinary field names and distinguish the explicitly excepted pseudo-header form.

requirements.quote:
*  A field value MUST NOT contain the zero value (ASCII NUL, 0x00),
      line feed (ASCII LF, 0x0a), or carriage return (ASCII CR, 0x0d) at
      any position.
requirements.condition: An implementation validates an HTTP/2 field value.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Allow ASCII NUL (0x00), LF (0x0a), or CR (0x0d) at any position in the field value.
requirements.why_checkable: Each prohibited byte can be inserted at different field-value positions and the implementation's rejection behavior observed.

requirements.quote:
*  A field value MUST NOT start or end with an ASCII whitespace
      character (ASCII SP or HTAB, 0x20 or 0x09).
requirements.condition: An implementation validates an HTTP/2 field value.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Allow a field value to start or end with ASCII SP (0x20) or HTAB (0x09).
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can independently place SP and HTAB at the beginning and end of a field value.

requirements.quote:
A request or response that contains a field that violates any of
   these conditions MUST be treated as malformed (Section 8.1.1).  In
   particular, an intermediary that does not process fields when
   forwarding messages MUST NOT forward fields that contain any of the
   values that are listed as prohibited above.
requirements.condition: A request or response contains a field violating any of the stated field-name or field-value conditions.
requirements.required_behavior: Classify the request or response as malformed.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can place each prohibited character pattern in a field and inspect malformed-message classification.

requirements.quote:
A request or response that contains a field that violates any of
   these conditions MUST be treated as malformed (Section 8.1.1).  In
   particular, an intermediary that does not process fields when
   forwarding messages MUST NOT forward fields that contain any of the
   values that are listed as prohibited above.
requirements.condition: An intermediary forwards messages without processing fields, and a field contains a value prohibited by the stated validation rules.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can send prohibited field bytes through a non-processing intermediary and inspect the forwarded message.

requirements.quote:
When a request message violates one of these requirements, an
   implementation SHOULD generate a 400 (Bad Request) status code (see
   Section 15.5.1 of [HTTP]), unless a more suitable status code is
   defined or the status code cannot be sent (e.g., because the error
   occurs in a trailer field).
requirements.condition: A request violates one of the field requirements, no more suitable status code is defined, and a status code can be sent.
requirements.why_checkable: A request with a generic field-syntax violation can be sent where a response remains possible, and the returned status inspected.

requirements.quote:
|  Note: Field values that are not valid according to the
      |  definition of the corresponding field do not cause a request to
      |  be malformed; the requirements above only apply to the generic
      |  syntax for fields as defined in Section 5 of [HTTP].
requirements.condition: A field value satisfies the generic field syntax but is invalid only according to the definition of its corresponding field.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Classify the request as malformed solely because of the field-specific value invalidity.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can use a generically well-formed but field-semantically invalid value and verify that generic malformed-message handling is not triggered solely for that reason.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint MUST NOT generate an HTTP/2 message containing
   connection-specific header fields.  This includes the Connection
   header field and those listed as having connection-specific semantics
   in Section 7.6.1 of [HTTP] (that is, Proxy-Connection, Keep-Alive,
   Transfer-Encoding, and Upgrade).  Any message containing connection-
   specific header fields MUST be treated as malformed (Section 8.1.1).
requirements.condition: An endpoint generates an HTTP/2 message.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Generate a message containing Connection, Proxy-Connection, Keep-Alive, Transfer-Encoding, Upgrade, or another connection-specific header field.
requirements.why_checkable: Generated HTTP/2 field blocks can be inspected for the enumerated connection-specific field names.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint MUST NOT generate an HTTP/2 message containing
   connection-specific header fields.  This includes the Connection
   header field and those listed as having connection-specific semantics
   in Section 7.6.1 of [HTTP] (that is, Proxy-Connection, Keep-Alive,
   Transfer-Encoding, and Upgrade).  Any message containing connection-
   specific header fields MUST be treated as malformed (Section 8.1.1).
requirements.condition: An HTTP/2 message contains a connection-specific header field.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can inject each enumerated connection-specific field and observe malformed-message classification.

requirements.quote:
The only exception to this is the TE header field, which MAY be
   present in an HTTP/2 request; when it is, it MUST NOT contain any
   value other than "trailers".
requirements.condition: An HTTP/2 request contains a TE header field.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the TE field when its value is "trailers".
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Allow the TE field to contain any value other than "trailers".
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can compare acceptance of the exact value "trailers" with rejection of other TE values.

requirements.quote:
An intermediary transforming an HTTP/1.x message to HTTP/2 MUST
   remove connection-specific header fields as discussed in
   Section 7.6.1 of [HTTP], or their messages will be treated by other
   HTTP/2 endpoints as malformed (Section 8.1.1).
requirements.condition: An intermediary transforms an HTTP/1.x message into HTTP/2.
requirements.required_behavior: Remove connection-specific header fields from the transformed message.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Retain connection-specific header fields in the resulting HTTP/2 message.
requirements.why_checkable: A transformation test can supply HTTP/1.x connection-specific fields and inspect whether they are absent from the HTTP/2 output.
